kHzPalmLoop.notes: Positions, ranges and normalling read from src/PalmLoop.cpp at tag 2.0.1, the installed version. The octave figure comes from the pitch sum in process(): the knob value plus 0.031360 octaves, so the default 8 gives 2^8.03136Hz, C4 at 261.63Hz. The square and triangle run at half the sawtooth frequency because the sign flip happens once per phase wrap; the sub sine is built from half the phase, so it is an octave down as well. Linear FM is only summed when the LIN FM jack is connected, and the phase increment is then clamped to one sample period either way.

Transposes both oscillators by seven semitones either way, in semitone steps
Transposes both oscillators anywhere within a semitone either way
Offsets oscillator B from the master pitch, one octave down to four octaves up, a frequency ratio of a half to sixteen times
Attenuates and inverts the EXP A input; the setting is cubed, and at full clockwise one volt there moves oscillator A by about one octave
Attenuates and inverts the LIN A input; the setting is cubed, and at full clockwise one volt there shifts oscillator A by about 1600Hz
Attenuates and inverts the EXP B input; the setting is cubed, and at full clockwise one volt there moves oscillator B by about one octave
Attenuates and inverts the LIN B input; the setting is cubed, and at full clockwise one volt there shifts oscillator B by about 1600Hz
Randomises the length of every cycle of oscillator A, from none at fully counter-clockwise to a whole cycle either way at fully clockwise, which turns its sawtooth into noise
The probability that oscillator A is restarted at each cycle end of oscillator B, from never at fully counter-clockwise to every time at fully clockwise; it starts fully counter-clockwise
Randomises the length of every cycle of oscillator B, from none at fully counter-clockwise to a whole cycle either way at fully clockwise, which turns its sawtooth into noise

kHzTachyonEntangler.notes: Read from src/TachyonEntangler.cpp at tag 2.0.1, the installed version. The exponential FM attenuverters run -1.7 to 1.7 and are cubed, then scaled by 0.2, giving about 0.98 octaves per volt at the extreme; the linear FM attenuverters run -11.7 to 11.7 and are cubed, giving about 1602Hz per volt. The chaos and sync modulation attenuverters run -0.1 to 0.1, so ten volts covers the whole 0 to 1 range of the knob they add to. Exponential and linear FM are each summed only while their own jack is connected. The maker's README calls oscillator B the slave; in the code either oscillator syncs the other, and the default knob settings are what make B the synced one. The square outputs run at half the sawtooth frequency, which the README states as well.

lines: Transposes and inverts a polyphonic V/OCT signal, with trigger inputs that switch the transposition and the inversion on and off
Transposes by whole octaves, four octaves down to four octaves up
Transposes by seven semitones either way, in semitone steps
Raises the transposition by a quarter tone, which puts quarter-tone intervals within reach of the two transpose knobs
Turns inversion on; with it off nothing is ever inverted, and with it on the incoming voltage is flipped about 0V before the transposition is added
A trigger flips the inversion between on and off while the INV button is on; with nothing patched here the inversion is applied the whole time that button is on
A trigger flips the transposition between applied and not applied; with nothing patched here the transposition is applied the whole time
The polyphonic V/OCT signal to transpose and invert, every channel treated the same way
The transposed and inverted signal, carrying as many channels as the input
kHzD_Inf.notes: Read from src/D_Inf.cpp at tag 2.0.1, the installed version. The transposition sum is octave plus 0.083333 per coarse step plus 0.041667 for the half-sharp button, so the button is exactly a quarter tone. Inversion is forced off whenever the INV button is off, whatever the INV input has done.
